title: Nepetin suppresses HBV-associated hepatocellular carcinoma metastasis by regulating the HBx/HIF-1alpha-mediated autophagy axis.
authors: Liao, Mianmian; Du, Haiyan; Zhong, Qiusheng; Zhang, Yu; Zhang, Yi; Wang, Zhijuan; Qin, Yiheng; Chen, Bo; Chen, Tuantuan; Zhang, Huanhuan; Yuan, Weiqu; Huang, Danping; Zhou, Hua; Tong, Guangdong
journal: Phytomedicine : international journal of phytotherapy and phytopharmacology
one_liner_zh: 研究黄酮类化合物Nepetin通过调控HBx/HIF-1alpha自噬轴抑制HBV相关肝癌转移，涉及分子对接但非蛋白质-DNA互作核心，方法仅浅层对接，与TF-DNA课题关联弱。
abstract: BACKGROUND: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) arising from chronic Hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection has a high metastatic potential, driven largely by the viral oncoprotein Hepatitis B Virus X Protein (HBx) and a hypoxic tumor microenvironment. Therapeutic strategies targeting these underlying oncogenic mechanisms remain an unmet clinical need. PURPOSE: Nepetin, a naturally occurring flavonoid with known anti-inflammatory and antitumor activities, has not been evaluated for efficacy against HBV-associated HCC metastasis. Therefore, this study aimed to investigate its antimetastatic potential and underlying molecular mechanisms. STUDY DESIGN: The antimetastatic effects and molecular targets of Nepetin were evaluated using complementary in vitro and in vivo models of HBV-associated HCC. METHODS: The antimetastatic effects of Nepetin were assessed in vitro using HBV-positive HCC cell lines and in vivo using an orthotopic liver xenograft model and a tail vein injection metastasis model. Mechanistic studies were conducted using western blotting, molecular docking, cellular thermal shift assay and surface plasmon resonance assays. RESULTS: Nepetin treatment significantly reduced migration and invasion of HBV-HCC cells in vitro by approximately 45% and 50%, respectively, at 10 microM, and suppressed intrahepatic and pulmonary metastasis in vivo, without apparent toxicity. Mechanistically, Nepetin disrupted the interaction between HBx and HIF-1alpha, leading to reduced hypoxia-inducible factor-1alpha (HIF-1alpha), thereby reducing HIF-1alpha protein stability and transcriptional activity and subsequently suppressed the downstream prometastatic autophagic flux. CONCLUSION: The findings identify Nepetin as a candidate compound that inhibits HBV-HCC metastasis by targeting the HBx/HIF-1alpha/autophagy signaling cascade. These findings provide a mechanistic rationale for targeting this pathway and support further evaluation of the translational potential of Nepetin in metastatic HBV-HCC.
abstract_zh: 背景：由慢性乙型肝炎病毒（Hepatitis B virus, HBV）感染引发的肝细胞癌（Hepatocellular carcinoma, HCC）具有高转移潜力，这主要归因于病毒癌蛋白乙型肝炎病毒X蛋白（Hepatitis B Virus X Protein, HBx）和缺氧肿瘤微环境。针对这些潜在致癌机制的治疗策略仍是未满足的临床需求。目的：Nepetin是一种天然类黄酮，已知具有抗炎和抗肿瘤活性，但尚未评估其对HBV相关HCC转移的疗效。因此，本研究旨在探讨其抗转移潜力及潜在分子机制。研究设计：使用互补的体外和体内HBV相关HCC模型，评估Nepetin的抗转移效果和分子靶点。方法：在体外使用HBV阳性HCC细胞系，在体内使用原位肝异种移植模型和尾静脉注射转移模型，评估Nepetin的抗转移效果。机制研究通过蛋白质印迹法、分子对接、细胞热位移分析和表面等离子体共振分析进行。结果：Nepetin处理在10微摩尔浓度下，显著减少HBV-HCC细胞体外的迁移和侵袭，分别约45%和50%，并抑制体内肝内和肺转移，且无明显毒性。机制上，Nepetin破坏了HBx与HIF-1α之间的相互作用，导致缺氧诱导因子-1α（hypoxia-inducible factor-1alpha, HIF-1alpha）减少，从而降低HIF-1α蛋白稳定性和转录活性，并随后抑制下游促转移的自噬通量。结论：研究结果将Nepetin鉴定为一种候选化合物，通过靶向HBx/HIF-1α/自噬信号级联抑制HBV-HCC转移。这些发现为靶向该通路提供了机制依据，并支持进一步评估Nepetin在转移性HBV-HCC中的转化潜力。
